report.title: When programmable processing-in-memory wins after the full data path is charged

budget_assessment.judgment: Within the 1,400-1,700-word, six-primary-URL, and one-table budget. It addresses end-to-end timing boundaries with representative wins and losses, separates hardware from simulation, and gives an explicitly labeled transferable checklist.

scope_and_novelty_assessment.judgment: Finite and substantive; accepted with source-context corrections.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.scope_coverage: Compares PrIM's measured UPMEM characterization, DIMES's transfer-inclusive extension, and uPIMulator's modeled mechanisms. The report covers transfer/setup boundaries, workload placement and result size, and persistent versus one-off use; it avoids aggregating results across different machines and baselines.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.overlap: No material overlap with R779's irregular gather/page behavior, R786's destination contention and reduction, R873's dense ASIC dataflow, or R877's geometric neighbor search. Those were used as indexed metadata boundaries only; their held report bodies were not read.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.novel_increment: A source-bounded comparison of programmable UPMEM-DPU results under kernel-only, transfer-inclusive, and simulation/model boundaries. The checklist is explicitly inference and is not a Strata or Arc recommendation.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.conclusion: Keep as a held collection; no current retrieval or repeat survey is recommended.

depth_and_applicability.judgment: Adequate detail and counterevidence for the assigned question.
depth_and_applicability.strengths: The table separates measured workloads, dataset/placement notes, baselines, and counted time. It includes an initial HST-S win, a persistent transfer-inclusive HST/TS result, and RED/SCAN/VA/SpMV losses after transfer. It distinguishes configuration costs from plotted transfer-inclusive results and calls out persistence and larger CPU baselines.
depth_and_applicability.limits: The numerical results apply to the cited UPMEM hosts, DPUs, SDK releases, and selected dataset sizes. The DIMES PDF's direct browser fetch timed out during review; relevant indexed text from the author-hosted primary PDF and the ACM DOI record were accessible. The report appropriately does not treat PIMulator simulations as hardware measurements or claim transfer to another accelerator.
depth_and_applicability.provenance_and_adoption: Research-only; no implementation, product source, local measurement, code adaptation, or adoption decision was proposed or inspected.

source_accuracy.status: All three assigned primary works and the main quantitative comparisons were checked. One workload scaling label is incorrect; SDK provenance should be made more explicit when reusing the transfer figures.
verified: PrIM arXiv v7: system sizes/clocks, Xeon E3-1225 v6 and Titan V baselines, HST-S 1.89x over Titan V on 640 DPUs, the 1536x1024 6 MB histogram input, 512K-element/2 MB TS input with 256-element queries, and RED/SCAN dataset values.

PrIM timing boundary: DPU plus inter-DPU synchronization is counted for UPMEM; CPU/GPU comparison uses kernel time, and host-to-GPU transfer is excluded. The 32 MB single-DPU transfer rates and 64-DPU peak parallel transfer rates match the paper.

DIMES 2023: 2,304 DPUs at 350 MHz with 16 tasklets, a four-thread Xeon Silver 4215 baseline, transfer-inclusive plotted bars, the -O2 CPU arm, and allocation/load measurements kept separate from plotted latency. The paper reports RED/SCAN/SpMV/VA losing after transfers and HST/TS retaining large advantages; its conclusion states 9 of 11 benchmarks favor the server CPU under its resource-aware accounting.

uPIMulator arXiv v3/HPCA 2024: 710 single-DPU validation points at 98.4% correlation and 12.0% MAE; 387 multi-DPU points at 83.6% correlation and 26.9% MAE; fixed-bandwidth CPU-DPU communication modeling; 14-stage in-order DPU model; and simulated GEMV results of 2.6x and 4.6x for the named design variants.
source_accuracy.limits: PrIM explicitly attributes transfer asymmetry to UPMEM SDK 2021.1.1; DIMES cites UPMEM SDK 2023.1.0. These are source-specific references, not a controlled cross-paper SDK comparison. The DIMES PDF text was retrieved through its indexed author-hosted document and cross-checked with the ACM record because direct PDF fetching timed out.

corrections.correction: The report labels RED's 50 MB and SCAN's 30 MB as per-DPU strong-scaling inputs. PrIM Table 3 lists 50/30 MB as the 1-DPU strong-scaling inputs; its 32-rank strong-scaling inputs are 3.1/1.9 GB, while 50/30 MB per DPU appears in the separate weak-scaling column. Replace the label and identify which scale is used for any workload comparison.

The report notes that transfer rates depend on host/SDK generation but omits the cited versions. PrIM explicitly attributes the directional transfer asymmetry to UPMEM SDK 2021.1.1; DIMES cites UPMEM SDK 2023.1.0. Preserve the version-specific context when reusing those rates, and do not imply a controlled cross-paper SDK comparison.

retrieval.retrieve_when: A concrete future research or measurement question asks for UPMEM offload accounting, data placement, or transfer/setup comparison; retrieve only the relevant section and apply R885-C1/C2.
preserve_caveats: PrIM CPU/GPU headline comparisons are kernel-only; UPMEM includes DPU plus inter-DPU synchronization but omits host transfer.
DIMES transfer-inclusive bars do not include the separately measured allocation/program-load costs; its output-aggregation boundary is not fully itemized.
PrIM transfer figures are host- and SDK-dependent; the cited SDK is 2021.1.1, while DIMES cites 2023.1.0.
RED/SCAN strong-scaling starting totals must not be labeled as weak-scaling per-DPU input sizes.
uPIMulator is modeled evidence; its future-architecture speedups are not measured UPMEM results.
These UPMEM results do not establish performance or adoption for GPUs, Intel Arc, SYCL, or Strata.
